v1.label: V1
v1.delegation: The eve built-in `agent` tool, with an outputSchema
v1.findings: The child agent sent all vendors in one final message

v2.label: V2
v2.modelPlane: Nebius Token Factory · one model for each job
v2.delegation: A declared `scout` subagent. Its tools are web search and record_vendor
v2.findings: The scout records each vendor immediately in Redis
v2.observability: A trace of each agent, LangSmith, and a live console
v2.evaluation: Three fixed data sets and five scripts
v2.guards: The record_vendor tool refuses bad data

changes.title: The research agents could send email
changes.old: V1 delegated research with the eve built-in `agent` tool. This tool starts a copy of the root agent. The copy gets the same tools as the root agent. One of those tools sends email to a vendor.
changes.new: V2 uses a declared subagent. Its name is `scout`. Its tools are web search and `record_vendor`, and nothing else. V2 also disables the built-in `agent` tool.
changes.why: A rule in the instructions does not remove a tool. The research agent kept the ability to send email. Only the absence of the tool prevents the action.
changes.result: The scout cannot send email. A later run showed the planner used both delegation paths: 10 `scout` calls and 3 `agent` calls. V2 disabled the built-in tool after that run.

star.situation: V1 produced good plans. No fault was visible. The research agents inherited every tool of the root agent, and one of those tools sends email to a real vendor.
star.task: Remove the ability to send email from the research agents. Do not remove the ability from the planner.
star.action: Move research into a declared subagent with two tools. Shadow the built-in `agent` tool with a tool that refuses.
star.result: The research agents have no email tool. The guarantee does not depend on the model.

changes.title: A cut-off agent lost all of its work
changes.old: V1 asked the child agent to send all vendors in one final message. The message used an outputSchema.
changes.new: V2 records each vendor immediately with `record_vendor`. The planner reads the records with `get_research`.
changes.why: One final message makes every vendor depend on the last token. A cut-off message loses all of them. Zero vendors also looks the same as an empty market.
changes.result: Work continues after a fault. A count of zero is now a fault that the planner can see. Measured: 3 to 4 vendors for each agent, and no cut-off agents.

star.situation: The child agent sent its vendors in one message at the end of its work. A cut-off message lost all of them.
star.task: Keep the work of an agent that stops early.
star.action: Add a `record_vendor` tool. The agent calls it after it verifies each vendor. Add `get_research` to read the records and to report the condition of each agent.
star.result: A cut-off agent keeps every vendor that it found before the fault. The planner runs one more agent for a category with zero vendors.

changes.title: The structured answer stopped the tool calls
changes.old: V1 and early V2 put an outputSchema on the child agent.
changes.new: V2 has no outputSchema on the scout.
changes.why: eve changes a schema fault into a failed session. A schema also blocks the tool calls of some models. The research is in Redis, so the answer of the agent is not necessary.
changes.result: The score moved from 10/22 (45%) to 52/53 (98%). All 10 agents failed with the schema. No agent failed after removal.

star.situation: V2 changed the scout model to a less expensive model. All 10 scout sessions failed. No agent recorded a vendor. The score was 10/22.
star.task: Find the cause. The less expensive model was one possible cause. The schema was another.
star.action: Read the trace of each failed session. Each session ended with OUTPUT_SCHEMA_NOT_FULFILLED. Some sessions failed before the first web search. Remove the outputSchema and return to the first model.
star.result: The score moved to 52/53. A later paper (arXiv 2606.25605) describes the same fault: a schema and tool calls together stop some open-weight models from calling tools.

changes.title: An email went to the wrong company
changes.old: V1 told the agent to use the web site of the vendor. V1 did not check the result.
changes.new: V2 refuses a source URL from a directory site. V2 also refuses an email address that does not agree with the name or the web site of the vendor.
changes.why: The instructions already forbade both faults. The model made both faults. A rule that the model can ignore is not a control.
changes.result: All later runs show 100% own-site sources and zero incorrect addresses. A test holds 12 real records from the run with the fault.

star.situation: The system recorded a caterer with the email address inquiries@hideseekmedia.com. That address belongs to a media company. The source was a directory page for a different company. The system sends email to real vendors.
star.task: Prevent an email to a company that the couple did not choose.
star.action: Add two refusals to `record_vendor`. The first refuses 20 known directory hosts. The second refuses an address whose domain does not agree with the vendor. Free mail addresses pass, because a small florist with a gmail address is normal.
star.result: The three bad records are refused. All nine good records still pass. Later runs record no directory sources and no incorrect addresses.

changes.title: Nobody could see what the agents did
changes.old: V1 had no trace store, no hook, and no instrumentation. The work of a child agent was not visible.
changes.new: V2 writes a trace of each agent to Redis. V2 sends spans to LangSmith. The app shows a live view of each agent.
changes.why: You cannot correct a fault that you cannot see. Each fault in this list was found in a trace.
changes.result: The console shows each agent, its model, its steps, its tools, its tokens, and its cost.

changes.title: Every cost was zero
changes.old: V1 showed no cost. V2 showed a cost of $0.00 for every agent.
changes.new: V2 reads the model identifier from the correct field. V2 removes the provider prefix before it reads the price table.
changes.why: eve reports the model in `RuntimeIdentity.modelId`. The code read `runtime.model`. The trace also adds a provider prefix to the identifier. The price table uses the identifier without the prefix.
changes.result: Cost is now correct for each step and each agent. The middle run costs $2.14. The most expensive run costs $6.07.

changes.title: No measurement of quality
changes.old: V1 had no evaluation. A change to the instructions had no measurable result.
changes.new: V2 has three fixed data sets and five scripts. The judge model is different from the model under test.
changes.why: A fixed data set makes a change measurable. A judge that is also the model under test moves the standard with the model.
changes.result: Reply understanding: 15/15. Research quality: 52/53. Schema reliability: 30/30 for the model in use.

changes.title: One model for all work
changes.old: V1 used one model for all work: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 through the Vercel AI Gateway.
changes.new: V2 uses Nebius Token Factory. V2 selects a model for each job: planner, scout, classifier, and judge.
changes.why: Each job has different requirements. A change of model must be a change of configuration, not a change of code.
changes.result: Two model changes were tested and refused. The measurements showed a 13% schema fault rate for one model, and 10 failed sessions for the other.
